252465346_6f956193.text: The orexin peptides, also called hypocretins, were discovered simultaneously by 2 research groups just over 2 decades ago. (Lecea et al., 1998)(Sakurai et al., 1998) The orexin peptides consist of 2 types, orexin-A and B, which are encoded by the hypocretin neuropeptide precursor gene and subsequently produced from the same precursor, prepro-orexin. Orexin-producing neurons are contained within the lateral, dorsomedial, posterior, and perifornical areas of the hypothalamus. (Lecea et al., 1998)(Sakurai et al., 1998)

252465346_577c2d28.text: However, orexin neurons extend a network of axonal projections which innervate numerous brain regions, ( ��, 2007)(Peyron et al., 1998) allowing a profound effect on complex physiological processes. Some of the densest orexinergic axonal projections synapse in wake-promoting brain areas such as the noradrenergic locus coeruleus, among others. ( ��, 2007)(Peyron et al., 1998) Orexin neurons receive additional input from the sleep-promoting regions, (14875802)(Yoshida et al., 2006) which contribute to the modulatory role of orexin in sleep/wake transitions. In addition to its clear impact on sleep, orexin impacts areas involved in sympathetic autonomic control, including the nucleus of the solitary tract, rostral ventrolateral medulla, and the parvocellular neurons of the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVN). ( ��, 2007)(Ciriello et al., 2003)(Date et al., 1999)(Machado et al., 2002) Many of these projections are reciprocated via afferent neural synapses on orexin- producing neurons from numerous autonomic and sleep/wakefulness related brain nuclei. (14875802)(Yoshida et al., 2006) The interconnectedness of orexin-producing neurons within both sleep and autonomic related brain regions indicate a crucial role of orexin as a link between insufficient sleep and impaired sympathetic control.
